instrument: assets/tests/_s3r11-interaction-runner.js, extended for R12 with: per-request sent/settled marks (so READ ROUNDS are visible, not just request counts), broad-cache getter instrumentation (so a table that is FETCHED but never READ is visible), a one-shot stall (so a read can be made to exceed its budget), and the Special Event Next path beside the Regular one.
harness_faults_found_and_fixed: The R11 fixture answered EVERY fcSummary slice request with EVERY model key, including fcSpecialEvents. Real slices carry one key set each (_FC_SLICE_KEYS_). With fcSpecialEvents always present the events slice could never be missing, so _fcEnsureEventSource_ could not be observed firing at all — the fixture hid the exact state this round changes.
fc_special_events was an empty fixture table, so an EMPTY existing-event picker could not be told apart from an UNREADABLE one. It now carries 24 rows.
what_is_authoritative: Request counts, read ROUNDS, and which broad-cache getters each path actually calls.
DOM outcomes: whether the existing-event picker is readable, whether a skeleton is stuck, whether any transport request is left open.
what_is_not: pollMs — Chrome virtual time, as recorded in the R11 evidence. Production milliseconds remain operator-owned; the operator figures in this round (~6 s Regular, ~37 s Special) are approximate and are deliberately NOT converted into benchmarks.

path_diff.TRUE_COLD_ROUNDS_POST: ceil(5/2) = 3, with the events slice concurrent
path_diff.note: The measured runs below show 4 extra requests / 2 rounds for Special because the harness opens the Regular builder first, which warms sku_details and marketplace_skus. The 6-table / 3-round figure is the declared list, and is what a session that goes straight to Special pays.

getters_called_during_special_open.why_it_matters: campaign_sku_lines is read only by _evtHydrateExisting_, which runs when the operator picks an EXISTING event. pricing_list is read only by resolveRegionalPricingContext, which runs when a SKU row is given a SKU. Neither is needed to open the builder — but both ARE needed later, so removing them from the cold path is a deferral, which is §11 territory and is proposed rather than implemented.

client_normalization_cost.measured_with: Node, real timers, the shipped normalizeOperationDb
client_normalization_cost.conclusion: CLIENT_NORMALIZATION is ruled OUT as the dominant segment by measurement, not by argument: at 40 000 campaign_sku_lines and 9 000 pricing rows the whole six-table set normalizes in about a third of a second. The same fixtures serialize to ~3.9 MB (mid) and ~20 MB (large) of JSON for the Special set versus ~0.78 MB / ~2.8 MB for the Regular set, a 5-7x ratio that tracks the operator's observed ~37 s vs ~6 s. The cost is the reads.

SRD_TIMEOUT_REFUSAL.refusalText: Couldn’t load regional details: No answer arrived within 60s. [action skuDetails.workspace.get · REQUEST_TIMEOUT · request REQ-C000013]. Ret

s11_variant_measurement_only.DISCLAIMER: MEASURED AND REVERTED. This variant drops campaign_sku_lines and pricing_list from the Special cold path. It is NOT committed and NOT shipped: §11 requires operator approval before deferring data out of the cold path. It exists so the proposal carries a number instead of an adjective.

sku_regional_timeout.why: The cause is a property of the Apps Script container and the network. A stub cannot produce it, and injecting a delay would only prove the timeout fires.
sku_regional_timeout.evidence: SRD_TIMEOUT_REFUSAL / SRD_TIMEOUT_RECOVERY above, driven by stalling one real read past the 60 s budget in a real browser.
